title: Zillion
subtitle: Infiltrating Planet X
summary: Zillion is Sega's exploration platform game, first released for Master System in Japan on 24 May 1987 alongside Tatsunoko's animated series.
body: Zillion is Sega's exploration platform game, first released for Master System in Japan on 24 May 1987 alongside Tatsunoko's animated series. J.J. infiltrates an enemy base on Planet X to collect five floppy disks and trigger its destruction. The mission unfolds through an interconnected underground complex, combining gunfire and platform movement with computer terminals and codes. Captured allies can join the operation, while returning to the surface provides a way to recover health. The base becomes a place to understand room by room before the final command can be carried out.

Capsules contain power-ups and the symbols needed for a room's four-part computer code. Breaking them and reading the contents allows the player to unlock another passage through its terminal. ID cards also govern access, while additional commands can disable traps or barriers. The process makes observation part of movement: clearing the enemies is only one step towards leaving the room. A stronger gun opens tougher capsules, so improving the weapon helps the investigation as well as the fighting, connecting upgrades to information that was previously out of reach.

Rescuing Apple and Champ makes them playable alongside J.J. Apple moves quickly but is weaker, while Champ trades speed for strength, giving the team different advantages within the same base. Their abilities can improve through collected upgrades. Tokuhiko Uwabo composed the music, and the weapon's design also connected the series to Sega's Light Phaser accessory. Zillion gives its fictional technology a practical role throughout the mission: the gun opens capsules, the capsules reveal information and the terminal turns that information into another route through the underground complex.
